turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Alright, vitals are in. Blood pressure one eighteen over seventy two, heart rate eighty eight. Ferritin from Tuesday is twelve, it's up on the screen.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Umm, screen just flipped. Say the pressure again?
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): One eighteen over seventy two. Pulse eighty eight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. What brought you in?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay so the reason I actually came, not the routine stuff, is my legs at night. They creep, like something is crawling under the skin, and I cannot sleep.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, wrong chart tab. Creep, like restless?

[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, restless, but it's this creeping in both calves the second I lie down, and if I don't move them it just builds till I get up. It's been about three weeks, since I hit twenty seven weeks, and I'm thirty weeks tomorrow, well actually today. I pace two or three times a night and then I'm useless at work.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She does pace. I'm up too, so yeah, two or three times.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling in the ankles?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. My sandals fit exactly the same, so I don't think it's real swelling.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Uh, while this password thing spins, family history. Diabetes, pressure, any of that?

[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): I'll just do everybody so you don't have to ask twice. My father had diabetes in his fifties, he was on pills for it, mother did not, she never had sugar or pressure, and another sister has pressure but no sugar, Denise, she takes a water pill. My brother is fine medically, he just complains about his knee from bowling.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Got it. And work, the hours, diet, exercise, drinking?

[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm a payroll clerk at the county office, thirty six hours a week, Monday through Thursday, Fridays off for stuff like this. Diet is oatmeal in the morning, a turkey sandwich at my desk, chicken or fish at night, and I keep the salt low because the midwife mentioned it. Exercise is walking the dog about twenty minutes after dinner if the legs allow, alcohol I stopped the week I found out I was pregnant, before that a glass of wine on the weekend, and I don't smoke, I never have.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The drive was the dramatic part. They shut the left lane on route nine and we sat there forever.

[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Twenty minutes at least, and the sky was this ugly yellow gray, one raindrop and then nothing. I was telling him about the new diner by the mall and we never even got to what I ordered last time.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yeah the weather's been weird all week. My kid's soccer got cancelled, lightning over the field.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Our neighbor's grandkid was gonna play in the yard and that got rained out. Little guy was stomping around in boots, furious.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Ha. Poor kid. Anyway.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Err, it wants the password again. What are you taking?

[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Folic acid, four hundred micrograms every morning, I have not missed one since the start of the pregnancy. And the iron, ferris sulfate, three hundred twenty five milligrams once a day with orange juice, the midwife started it when the ferritin came back low. I keep the bottles by the kettle so I actually see them.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Wait, say the iron dose again. I think I typed two twenty five.
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Three hundred twenty five. Once a day. Not two twenty five.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, three twenty five. Ferritin was twelve, that's low, and low iron can make the legs creep like this in pregnancy.

[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Which explains the days, honestly. I'm exhausted, I could fall asleep on the keyboard, same three weeks, and I set a second alarm so I don't miss the bus. It's embarrassing but that's where I am.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any headache, change in vision, pain up under the ribs?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No headache, vision is the same, nothing up under the ribs.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking restless legs, provisional, tied to the low iron while you're pregnant. Doesn't sound like preeclampsia.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep the iron once a day, don't double it. When the creep starts, get up and walk a minute, and try not to nap after four.

[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): The midwife already booked me next Thursday at ten, the regular check, I almost said thirty two weeks but no, I'm thirty now, it's just the routine visit. I'll bring the iron bottle so she sees the three twenty five.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, keep that Thursday visit. I'll see you back here in four weeks, reception already put it on the book.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you. I know I over-explain, I just wanted the legs and the sleep and the family stuff all in one place.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine. We're good if the note saves.

spec.situation: Pregnant woman at 30 weeks with creeping legs at night and poor sleep; ferritin discussed; takes folic acid and iron; midwife check booked.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Ferritin lab was completed, but transcript does not say nurse requested it.
Next Thursday at ten was already booked by the midwife, not planned by the doctor.
bad.text: Follow-up consultation (action_type=follow_up, status=planned, responsible_person=doctor, time_reference=value: next Thursday at ten)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: no real ankle swelling; patient said sandals fit the same and she does not think it is real swelling.
Family history: mother had neither diabetes nor high blood pressure.
Family history detail: father's diabetes began in his fifties and he was treated with pills.
Family history detail: sister Denise has high blood pressure and takes a diuretic ('water pill').
Symptom detail: restless/creeping sensation builds if she does not move her legs, leading her to get up and pace.
Functional impact of symptoms: she is 'useless at work' and sets a second alarm so she does not miss the bus due to exhaustion.
Follow-up detail recorded incorrectly: next Thursday at 10 is the already-booked routine midwife visit, not a follow-up with this doctor.
Plan/follow-up detail: patient was instructed to bring the iron bottle to the midwife so she can verify the 325 mg dose.
Assessment detail: doctor stated it does not sound like preeclampsia.
